features.featureTitle: In the frontend UserView, redesign the Single Comment Generator section to match the uploaded screenshot exactly: (1) a card with a blue gradient icon (sparkle/star), title 'Single Comment Generator', subtitle 'Generate one comment per list (one per device)'; (2) a 'Select Comment List' dropdown showing only unlocked lists for the selected app/event (keep the existing App/Event selector above it); (3) an 'Available Comments' display box showing the dynamic count fetched from the backend's `getAvailableCount` query for the selected list — the number must reflect real stored data, not a hardcoded value; (4) a lock notice box (blue tinted, with sparkle icon) showing 'You have already generated a comment for this list on this device.' when the device has already claimed a comment from the selected list; (5) a 'Generate Single Comment' button with a blue-to-teal gradient matching the screenshot, disabled (and showing the lock notice) if the device has already claimed a comment from this list. On successful generation, display the generated comment text with a Copy button below the card. On 'No comments left' error, show an 'Out of comments' badge instead.

In the frontend, on app load, ensure a persistent deviceId exists: read from localStorage key 'deviceId'; if missing, generate one via `crypto.randomUUID()` and store it back in localStorage. Pass this deviceId to the `generateComment` backend call. After a successful generation, store the claim in localStorage as a record keyed by listId so the UI can immediately show the lock notice without an extra backend round-trip on re-render.

Add an Admin Metrics section inside the Admin > Comments sub-tab (or as a separate 'Metrics' sub-section within the Admin panel). For each comment list, display a card showing: list name, Total / Used / Available counts (all dynamic from the backend `getListMetrics` query), a horizontal progress bar (Used/Total fill percentage), and a pure SVG/CSS donut chart visualizing Used (filled arc) vs Available (unfilled arc) using stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset on an SVG circle element. No Recharts or other chart library may be added. All numbers must come from real backend data with zero hardcoded values.
